agenda.title: Problem Statement
agenda.detail: What we set out to solve

detailPage.description: It follows the structure most departments expect, from problem statement and literature survey to architecture, results and future scope.
It moves from problem to solution, demo, traction and the ask — the order judges and investors expect.
It is built for dense academic content, so research questions, methods, findings and references stay readable from the back of the room.
It gives leadership a clear story: summary first, then performance, priorities and the decisions required.
It structures clinical content clearly, from history and investigations to management, outcomes and learning points.
It covers everything an audience needs on the day: programme, tracks, schedule, venue and organisers.

detailPage.description: A decision-ready capstone proposal with a bounded problem, feasibility checks, work packages, risks and measurable acceptance criteria.

authoredSlides.title: Scope and exclusions
body: Include a three-room pilot using an agreed meter data feed.
Provide weekly exceptions with an explanation and suggested investigation.
Exclude billing, automated switching and campus-wide deployment from the first release.

authoredSlides.title: Success criteria
authoredSlides.subtitle: Define what the review panel can verify
body:
Data quality
Document missing readings and reject impossible values.

Usefulness
Ask facilities staff to assess the relevance of each alert.

Traceability
Explain the baseline behind every exception.

Deliverability
Demonstrate the complete pilot within the agreed term.

authoredSlides.title: Options and feasibility
authoredSlides.subtitle: Compare realistic routes before committing to a build

authoredSlides.title: Data and access plan
body: Identify the meter owner and obtain permission before collecting readings.
Keep room identifiers separate from personal information; this proposal does not require individual tracking.
Record the sampling interval, retention period and process for reporting missing data.

authoredSlides.title: Risks and mitigations
authoredSlides.subtitle: Assign an owner and review these risks each week
table: Use a documented synthetic feed for prototyping
Add validation and a visible data-quality status
Review changes against the agreed success criteria

authoredSlides.title: Approval requested
body: Approve the three-room pilot scope and the proposed evaluation plan.
Nominate a facilities contact and confirm access to a sample meter feed.
Agree the first review date and the evidence required to continue.

authoredSlides.title: References and assumptions
body: Add the meter documentation and any campus energy-policy sources you actually consulted.
List the assumptions that still need a sponsor or supervisor to confirm.
Replace illustrative scores and durations with your team's verified estimates.

detailPage.description: A structured literature review with a reproducible search strategy, screening criteria, an evidence matrix, quality appraisal and a defensible research gap.

authoredSlides.title: Search strategy
body: Specify the scholarly databases searched and the date each search was run.
Record the full query strings, synonyms, publication window and language limits.
Track citation chaining separately so another reviewer can reproduce your process.

authoredSlides.title: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
authoredSlides.subtitle: Tailor and register these criteria before screening
table: Cloud-only monitoring without an edge comparison

authoredSlides.title: Evidence extraction matrix
authoredSlides.subtitle: Populate only from papers you have read; no citations are invented here

authoredSlides.title: Quality appraisal
authoredSlides.subtitle: Judge confidence before comparing headline numbers
body:
Validity
Does the evaluation answer the stated question?

Reproducibility
Are code, data and settings available?

Comparability
Are hardware and datasets sufficiently similar?

Transferability
Could the approach work beyond the test site?

authoredSlides.title: Cross-study synthesis
body: Group findings by device constraints, sensing approach, evaluation setting and deployment needs.
Separate consistent findings from disagreements and explain the likely source of each difference.
Avoid ranking models by accuracy when they were tested on incompatible datasets.

authoredSlides.title: The research gap
body: State the missing evidence, rather than simply claiming that few papers exist.
Connect the gap to a practical decision that the current evidence cannot support.
Propose a bounded next study with outcomes that would reduce that uncertainty.

authoredSlides.title: References and review limitations
body: Add full citations and links or DOIs for every included study.
Explain database coverage, publication bias and any single-reviewer limitations.
Keep the search log and exclusion reasons available as an appendix.

detailPage.description: An experiment report that separates objectives, apparatus, procedure, raw observations, analysis, uncertainty and a conclusion supported by measured evidence.

authoredSlides.title: Apparatus and measurement points
authoredSlides.subtitle: Insert your annotated apparatus photograph or schematic
body: Identify the heater, sample, insulation and temperature sensors.
Label dimensions, sensor positions and the direction of heat flow.

authoredSlides.title: Variables and controls
authoredSlides.subtitle: Record units and the reason for each controlled variable
table: Record at a defined steady-state condition
Keep constant or record any change

authoredSlides.title: Safety and setup checks
body: Follow the laboratory's approved procedure and supervisor instructions for the apparatus.
Document the equipment checks and operating limits specified for your experiment.
Record any departure from the approved setup before interpreting the observations.

authoredSlides.title: Observation sheet
authoredSlides.subtitle: Enter raw observations here; do not substitute illustrative chart data

authoredSlides.title: Analysis and uncertainty
body: Show the equation used to connect the measured variables, defining every symbol and unit.
Separate instrument resolution, repeated-trial variation and possible systematic effects.
Compare the observed trend with the hypothesis without claiming more precision than the measurements support.

authoredSlides.title: Error sources and improvements
authoredSlides.subtitle: Support each explanation with observations from your own run
table: Apply and report a consistent stability criterion

authoredSlides.title: Conclusion and lab references
body: Answer the experimental question using your measured trend and uncertainty.
State what the experiment does not establish and the most useful next measurement.
Cite the apparatus manual, course method and sources used in the analysis.

Owned
Describe the components you personally designed or implemented.

Collaborated
Credit the mentor and colleagues involved in decisions.

Reviewed

Outside scope

authoredSlides.title: Implementation walkthrough

body: Demonstrate the journey from request intake to an owner update.

authoredSlides.title: Skills developed

Describe a communication or prioritisation lesson from working with the team.
Explain what you would do differently on a similar assignment.

detailPage.description: A placement portfolio that links skills to evidence, walks through a flagship project, explains a decision and prepares clear interview discussion points.

authoredSlides.title: About me and target role
body: Introduce your degree, current focus and the type of role you are seeking.
Name two or three strengths that you can demonstrate with project evidence.
Add a professional contact method and links you are comfortable sharing.

authoredSlides.title: Skills backed by evidence
authoredSlides.subtitle: Replace generic proficiency ratings with specific examples

authoredSlides.title: Project demonstration
authoredSlides.subtitle: Add your own screenshot or demo storyboard
body: Explain the input, the action and the result a user sees.
Point to the code or artifact that demonstrates your individual contribution.

authoredSlides.title: One design decision
body: State a real trade-off you encountered and the constraints that mattered.
Compare the alternatives you considered and explain why you chose one.
Describe what you would revisit if usage, data or team size changed.

authoredSlides.title: Reliability and testing evidence
authoredSlides.subtitle: Show how you tested the work instead of claiming it is bug-free

authoredSlides.title: Collaboration and reflection
body: Describe a specific code review, feedback conversation or team coordination example.
Credit collaborators and distinguish your work from shared outputs.
Name one mistake, the correction and the lesson you now apply.

authoredSlides.title: Interview discussion prompts
body: Which part of my project would you like to inspect or see demonstrated?
What constraints would change my approach to this problem?
Which skill should I strengthen for the responsibilities of this role?

detailPage.description: An industrial-visit report built around observable processes, permitted evidence, a comparison with classroom concepts and clear limits on what a short visit can establish.

authoredSlides.title: Visit purpose and context
body: Name the host organisation, visit date and participating class or group.
Explain the learning objectives agreed with the faculty and host.
Describe the portion of the facility visited and any access limits.

authoredSlides.title: Annotated site observations
authoredSlides.subtitle: Use photographs or sketches that the host has permitted you to share
body: Label the process stage, observation location and relevant equipment.
Separate what you directly observed from what the host explained.

authoredSlides.title: Observation log
authoredSlides.subtitle: Use dated notes and attribute explanations to their source

authoredSlides.title: Classroom concept and site practice
authoredSlides.subtitle: Compare carefully; a short visit is not a formal compliance assessment

authoredSlides.title: Learning points and limitations
body: Describe the strongest connection between a course concept and a permitted observation.
Record what was not visible or could not be verified during the visit.
Propose a follow-up question that would deepen understanding without exposing confidential information.

authoredSlides.title: Acknowledgements and sources
body: Thank the host team and faculty who made the visit possible.
List the permitted handouts, course references and sources actually used.
Confirm that images and process details are approved for academic sharing.

authoredSlides.title: Chosen experiments
authoredSlides.subtitle: Each experiment should produce evidence for a decision
body:
Hypothesis
State the behaviour or outcome expected to change.

Measure
Choose an observable signal and an evaluation window.

Boundary
Limit the users, workflow or investment involved.

Decision rule
Define when to continue, change or stop.

authoredSlides.title: Action register
authoredSlides.subtitle: Confirm ownership in the session before closing

authoredSlides.title: Review cadence and guardrails
body: Schedule short evidence reviews and a final decision review before the planning window closes.
Record the limits on time, budget and customer disruption that must not be exceeded.
Escalate new information that changes the decision's assumptions or expected value.
